I was once asked in an interview what my relationship to work was. Not my work ethic etc, that exact phrase.

In terms of food though, it is a phrase I've heard used from a young age, much the same way as I would have heard the general philosophical phrase of "your relationship with the world". This goes a little against my first reply, but I've thought about it a bit more since. It was always used as a sort of descriptor for how things fit into your life, or how I felt I fit in a dynamic situation.

For instance, my relationship to the world around me is mainly healthy. I have many experiences, positive and negative, that shape me and I try to strive for a symbiotic relationship where I either better the environment around me or at least reduce how destructive my presence could be.

My relationship with work is healthy. I work to live, I don't live to work. I enjoy and take pride in my work but ultimately it is there to help me achieve my own personal goals and ambitions.

My relationship with food is also healthy. I eat to live, not live to eat. I eat to fuel myself so I can enjoy my day, I don't eat enough to make myself lethargic, or to little that I am uncomfortable.

My relationship with cousin A is healthy. I meet him when we both have the opportunity, we both enjoy the others company and we move on with our respective lives in between meetings. My relationship with cousin B is toxic. She demands all of my attention at all times. She doesn't want groups of people to distract me from her. She makes me feel anxious when we are apart by ensuring that she is constantly on my mind. She makes me believe that I can't survive without her and limiting our interactions to the same amount as cousin A would be unhealthy.
